title: The Robin
phrases: a round body on thin legs

doing.t: is puffed up into a round ball
is singing with its head tipped back
is tilting its head to one side
is looking at a crumb of cheese
is shaking out its wet feathers after a bath

close: Just the robin, close enough to see where the orange breast meets the grey.
Only the robin, round and plump, in the middle of the page.

roles.main: for the orange-red breast and face
roles.dark: for the eye, the beak and the shadow under the wing
roles.light: for the white belly and the shine in the eye
roles.accent: for the blue-grey edging around the breast

firstMark: Start with the eye: one round dot of {dark}, leaving a pinprick of paper for the shine.
Start with the curve of the breast in one smooth line of {main}.

title: The Wren
phrases: a short tail sticking straight up
a pale stripe over the eye

doing.t: is singing with its tail sticking straight up
is creeping along with its head down
is calling out with its wings half open

close: Just the wren, drawn large enough to show the fine stripes on its wings.
Only the wren, very small, in the middle of a big white page.

roles.main: for the warm brown back and wings
roles.dark: for the fine stripes and the eye
roles.light: for the pale stripe over the eye
roles.accent: for the pinkish legs

firstMark: Start with the tail: three short strokes of {main}, pointing up.
Start with the eye: a single dot of {dark}, with the pale stripe above it left as bare paper.

roles.dark: for the eye, the eye stripe and the dark chin
roles.light: for the white cheeks
roles.accent: for the blue cap

firstMark: Start with the dark stripe through the eye in one sharp line of {dark}.
Start with the head: a small circle drawn lightly in {main}.
